item.title: SAKA Museum Traces the Living Tradition of Kamasan Painting in Its First Temporary Exhibition
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
SAKA Museum at AYANA Bali has opened its first temporary exhibition with KAMASAN: The Noble Tradition of Balinese Painting, an expansive look at one of Bali’s most distinctive artistic traditions. Running through May 30, 2027, the exhibition brings together more than 30 works spanning the late 19th century to today, including ritual cloths, palm-leaf works, an astrological calendar and paintings preserved by the families of Kamasan masters. Rooted in the village of Kamasan and closely connected to Balinese-Hindu ritual, the tradition is recognizable for its highly codified figures, elaborate linework and connection to the visual language of wayang kulit.

Rather than treating Kamasan as a historical art form frozen in time, the exhibition places classical works alongside contemporary artists who are pushing its visual vocabulary into new territory. Curated by Farah Wardani and Made Chandra, the exhibition explores hereditary master painters, the women who have sustained the tradition, and a younger generation using Kamasan imagery to consider identity, ecology, technology and collective memory. The result is a portrait of a tradition that has survived not by remaining unchanged, but by continually finding ways to speak to the present.

The Curated Take:
KAMASAN offers a particularly meaningful way to encounter Balinese culture because the paintings are inseparable from the beliefs, rituals, stories and communities that shaped them. The decision to give contemporary practitioners equal footing with historic works also makes this more than a survey of traditional art. It invites visitors to consider what cultural preservation actually looks like when a living tradition is allowed to evolve.

item.title: Mulia Bali’s “A Night in Elysium” Brings a Grand Finale to the 2026 Festive Season
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Mulia Bali is turning the holiday season into a full resort experience, with Christmas celebrations, family programming, festive dining and a lavish New Year’s Eve finale planned for 2026. Set along the shores of Nusa Dua, the resort’s festivities culminate December 31 with “A Night in Elysium,” a gala in the Grand Ballroom featuring international performers, elaborate dining and a midnight countdown designed to carry the celebration into 2027.

The evening’s entertainment brings together The Starlets, whose performers have appeared at major international events and in West End productions including Hamilton and TINA – The Tina Turner Musical, with Australian live band Fiction. Across the wider festive calendar, guests can choose from Christmas Eve and Christmas Day feasts, countdown dinners at the resort’s restaurants and a kids program of creative workshops and holiday activities. Family packages, breakfast-inclusive direct-booking benefits and a dining gift-card promotion add further incentives for a holiday stay.

The Curated Take:
For travelers looking to make the holiday season an actual destination experience rather than simply a change of scenery, Bali offers an appealing combination of tropical surroundings and traditional year-end celebration. Mulia’s program is particularly geared toward multigenerational travelers, pairing a substantial entertainment lineup and gala atmosphere with dedicated children’s programming and multiple dining options.

item.title: Grupo Lomas Celebrates 45 Years by Putting Travel Advisors at the Heart of Its Story
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For 45 years, Grupo Lomas has built its presence in Mexico alongside the travel professionals who have connected generations of travelers with the Mexican Caribbean. That relationship took center stage during Lomas Appreciation Week (LAW) 2026, which brought 178 travel advisors together with tour operators from across North America, South America, the United Kingdom and Europe. The gathering also marked the first participation of MICE professionals and saw increased representation from Mexican advisors, reflecting the changing breadth of the travel industry and Grupo Lomas’ advisor community.

Held primarily at El Dorado Royale, the week offered attendees a behind-the-scenes look at the group’s hospitality portfolio, from gastronomy and beach experiences to family-focused entertainment at Nickelodeon Hotels & Resorts Riviera Maya. The program combined business updates and professional development with distinctly Mexican experiences, including the Legacy 45 Gastronomic Market and a playful Super Sliming at Aqua Nick. The week concluded with the LAW Awards, recognizing travel professionals across sales, specialization and wedding travel, while special honors highlighted relationships that have stretched across different stages of Grupo Lomas’ 45-year history.

The Curated Take:
For an industry built on relationships, LAW offers a useful reminder that the travel advisor remains an important part of how destinations and hospitality brands reach travelers. What makes the gathering particularly interesting is its blend of recognition and immersion: advisors aren’t simply being thanked for selling the product, they are being invited to experience the people, food, properties and experiences they ultimately recommend to their clients.

item.title: ANA Makes Perth More Accessible From Tokyo With Daily Flights
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Travel between Japan and Western Australia is about to become considerably easier, with All Nippon Airways increasing its direct Tokyo-Perth service from three flights per week to daily operations beginning October 25, 2026. The expanded schedule will run through March 27, 2027, responding to growing visitor demand from Japan and strengthening one of the key international air links into Western Australia.

The additional frequency is significant for a destination as geographically removed from many of its international markets as Western Australia. Perth now sits at the end of a network of 22 nonstop international routes, giving travelers from Japan and beyond more flexibility when planning a visit to experience the state’s wine regions, coastlines, wilderness and increasingly sophisticated cultural scene.

The Curated Take:
For a destination where distance has historically been part of the allure and the challenge, air connectivity matters. Daily Tokyo service makes Western Australia easier to incorporate into a Japan-Australia itinerary and gives Japanese travelers greater flexibility to explore beyond Australia’s more familiar eastern cities.

item.title: WWE Makes Perth a Three-Year Destination for Wrestling Fans
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Perth is about to become a recurring stop on the global WWE calendar, with a new three-year agreement bringing three WWE Weekend Takeovers to Western Australia between 2026 and 2028. The first arrives in December 2026, with Friday Night SmackDown on December 11, Wrestlepalooza: Perth on December 12 and Monday Night Raw on December 14 at RAC Arena. The surrounding festivities will extend beyond the arena with a WWE Superstore, fan meet-and-greets and community events, turning the weekend into a citywide experience for visiting fans.

For Western Australia, the deal adds another major international event to Perth’s growing calendar while giving travelers a reason to build a trip around the spectacle. The combination of headline entertainment and destination experiences makes this more than a single night at an arena, particularly for fans traveling internationally to experience WWE in Australia.

The Curated Take:
Major sporting and entertainment events can fundamentally change how travelers experience a city, and Perth is increasingly giving visitors reasons to plan around the calendar rather than simply the destination. For WWE fans, three consecutive days of programming offer an unusually easy excuse to turn a live event into a Western Australian getaway.

item.title: Sal Salis Ningaloo Reef Reimagines Barefoot Luxury for 2027
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Sal Salis Ningaloo Reef is preparing to enter a new chapter, with a major refurbishment set to transform the eco-luxury camp before it reopens in late March 2027. Tucked among the dunes of Western Australia’s Cape Range National Park and just steps from the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Ningaloo Reef, the 16-tent retreat will introduce redesigned Wilderness Tents with private ensuite bathrooms, marine-inspired interiors and furnishings chosen to reflect the colors and textures of the surrounding coastline.

Designed by Woods Bagot, the refurbishment extends beyond the accommodations to reshape the guest experience throughout the camp. A refreshed reception will lead into a new central sundeck and lounge, creating a social heart for the property, while a new dining area with banquette seating and an all-inclusive open bar adds another gathering point. The culinary offering will also be refined around seasonal, locally sourced produce, with Western Australian wines and regional beers included. Guests will continue to explore the landscape through guided gorge walks, snorkeling, kayaking and stand-up paddleboarding, with optional whale shark and humpback whale swims offering encounters with Ningaloo’s marine life.

The Curated Take

Sal Salis has always made its setting the centerpiece of the stay, and the refurbishment appears designed to strengthen rather than compete with that proposition. Reclaimed timber, woven details and materials selected to weather naturally connect the interiors to the coastal environment, while the new communal spaces give guests more ways to gather between adventures. It is a thoughtful interpretation of barefoot luxury, where comfort is elevated without losing the sense that you are living lightly within a remarkable wilderness.

item.title: National Scenic Byway Day Invites Travelers to Rediscover America by Road
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
September 22 will mark the first annual National Scenic Byway Day, a new observance encouraging travelers to explore the scenic, historic and culturally significant roads that connect communities across the United States. The timing is particularly notable in 2026, which also marks the nation’s 250th birthday and the centennial of the U.S. Numbered Highway System. For travelers drawn to road trips, the day offers a reason to slow down, leave the major highways behind and experience the places and stories found along America’s scenic routes.

Among the country’s standout byways is the 444-mile Natchez Trace Parkway, stretching through Mississippi, Alabama and Tennessee. The route combines sweeping landscapes with archaeological sites, historic markers, recreational opportunities and access to small communities, tracing layers of history from Indigenous homelands and early travel routes to the modern road trip. Travelers can mark National Scenic Byway Day by planning a scenic drive, visiting a byway community, exploring local museums and historic sites, or building a longer itinerary around one of America’s designated scenic routes.

The Curated Take

There is something especially appealing about a travel day built around the idea that getting there can be part of the experience. Scenic byways offer a slower form of American travel, where landscapes, local history and small communities become part of the itinerary rather than scenery passed at highway speed. National Scenic Byway Day arrives as a timely invitation to rediscover that kind of journey.

item.title: Barcelona’s SIPS Brings Its World-Class Cocktail Culture to Las Vegas
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Caesars Palace is bringing a taste of Barcelona’s celebrated cocktail scene to Las Vegas this fall as SIPS Drinkery House takes over VISTA Cocktail Lounge from October 31 through December 31. Founded by bartenders Simone Caporale and Marc Álvarez, the Eixample bar was named The World’s Best Bar in 2023 by The World’s 50 Best Bars and has remained among the global top three in the two years since. Its limited-time Las Vegas residency coincides with Caesars Palace’s 60th anniversary.

SIPS is known for putting flavor and technique ahead of convention, pairing familiar ingredients with inventive preparation and playful presentation. At VISTA, guests will encounter signature creations including the Purple Rain, a contemporary take on a whiskey sour combining bourbon with wild sour honey and beetroot, and the Mosaic, which pairs pisco brandy with aromatic woods from the Amazon rainforest and arrives in a painted glass inspired by Barcelona’s modernist art movement. The collaboration offers a rare opportunity to experience the work of one of Barcelona’s most influential cocktail destinations without leaving the Strip.

The Curated Take

Las Vegas has long borrowed from the world’s great dining cities, but this collaboration feels particularly well suited to the city’s appetite for spectacle. SIPS brings something more interesting than a familiar European name: a distinct cocktail philosophy in which the drink itself remains the focus, while technique, glassware and presentation become part of the experience.

item.title: Four Seasons Resort Bali at Sayan Reframes the Riverside Suite Experience
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Four Seasons Resort Bali at Sayan has unveiled the first seven suites in its sustainability-led refresh, introducing five Premier Duplex Suites and two Premier Family Suites that bring a contemporary interpretation to the resort’s signature relationship with the Ayung River valley. Created with Hirsch Bedner Associates (HBA), the redesigned spaces pair floor-to-ceiling views with hand-loomed textiles, locally crafted details, natural materials and a refined residential feel. Pale, earthy tones echo Ubud’s rice terraces, while dark stained teak grounds the interiors and integrated smart technology remains intentionally unobtrusive.

The 85-square-metre Premier Duplex Suite unfolds across two levels, with a river-facing living and dining area, teak-and-textile bedroom and private sun terrace designed for lingering. The Premier Family Suite takes a more tailored approach to multigenerational stays, placing a dedicated children’s room at the center of the experience while giving parents a generous living space overlooking the valley. Sustainability is embedded in the renovation itself, with the existing framework refurbished rather than rebuilt, locally sourced materials selected for longevity where possible, and energy-efficient lighting and next-generation air conditioning incorporated into the design.

The Curated Take

Sayan’s appeal has always been rooted in the feeling of being immersed in the landscape rather than simply looking at it. These first reimagined suites build on that idea without abandoning the resort’s distinctive architecture or Balinese character. The result is less a wholesale reinvention than a considered evolution, with the river, craftsmanship and sense of place remaining the defining elements.
